description: ExecutionTarget contract + DockerCompose compatibility adapter — the first buildable slice of EPIC #731 (brain/hands decoupling). Ratifies the Phase-0 boundary in a durable RFC, defines a provider-neutral capability-oriented execution contract with no Docker nouns, implements Docker Compose as its first adapter by delegating to .oh/scripts/docker-compose.sh, routes `oh sandbox`/`oh shell` through it, and proves zero behavior change via unchanged lifecycle tests, a --print-argv equivalence case, and a new tier-A probe. Anchor issue #733; Refs #731 (never Closes — epics do not close on one PR). WHY NOW (not a premature abstraction): the second implementation is scheduled, not hypothetical — EPIC #731's P0 explicitly schedules the Sysbox execution target as the NEXT slice after this one; #732 (durable sessions, needs execution.attached/execution.released off attach()) and #734 (credentials / capability separation, needs HarnessAuthState split from ExecutionState) are OPEN, real issues that consume this exact seam; openharness-cloud#104 is the third consumer and the reason the workspace stance is ratified in an RFC; and the Captain approved this scope on 2026-08-10, recorded in .oh/memory/2026-08-10/log.md (the spec-plan / spec-critique entries for this slug carry the approved scope and routing) — legs 1-3 are the load-bearing ones. ROLLBACK: single PR, revert-safe via `git revert` — additive files plus two in-place refactors, no persisted state, no migration, no config key/CLI flag/env var, no on-disk format change, so reverting the merge commit fully restores prior behavior with no operator cleanup. NON-GOAL (post-merge): rfc-brain-hands-boundary.md becomes the SOLE source of truth for Phase-0 boundary decisions — there is no obligation to keep archived task-folder content consistent with it, and no obligation to reopen this PRD when the RFC is later amended; future work cites and amends the RFC. NON-GOAL: no async attach() migration (that is a contractVersion 2 change, separately reviewed).

userStories.title: Ratify the Phase-0 brain/hands boundary in the RFC layer
userStories.description: As an architect consuming EPIC #731 from #732, #734, or openharness-cloud#104, I want the Phase-0 boundary decisions written down in a durable citable RFC so downstream slices build against one contract instead of re-deriving the boundary. Gated first: US-002..US-005 make design choices that are only defensible once the boundary is written.
acceptanceCriteria: Create .oh/docs/rfcs/rfc-brain-hands-boundary.md
It contains a brain/hands responsibility table naming ralph, cron, autopilot, and memory as brain
It states the eval split as a capability RULE (executes-in-environment = hands vs reads-repo-files = brain), not an enumerated list of evals
It defines all four state classes by name: WorkspaceState, ExecutionState, HarnessAuthState, SessionState
It documents the Hermes known-violation of the state taxonomy explicitly

It states the workspace stance `workspace: {hostRoot, targetRoot}` and that identical-path mapping (hostRoot === targetRoot) is the ONLY supported Phase-0 worktree config, with non-identical mapping documented as unsupported

It explicitly calls the two-field workspace shape SPECULATIVE: in Phase-0 only the degenerate equal case is legal, so the second field carries permission not semantics; the Sysbox slice is expected to give it semantics or collapse it to one field

Its header contains an AUTHORITY CLAUSE: 'This file is the sole authority for Phase-0 brain/hands boundary decisions. Do not restate its content in future PRDs, task folders, or wiki entries — cite it.'

It records the attach() synchrony decision and its migration path: attach() is synchronous in contractVersion 1 because the process-runner seam is spawnSync-based and attach is a blocking terminal handoff; a future contractVersion 2 (Sysbox or #732) may make it async and migrate runShell plus its assertions as a separately-reviewed change
Amend .oh/docs/rfcs/rfc-runtime-support.md § Purpose (~line 13) to say the host Docker socket is opt-in and off by default, and the image ships the docker CLI but no dockerd
Amend .oh/docs/rfcs/rfc-runtime-support.md § 1 axis A1 row (~line 27) with the same correction
Amend .oh/docs/rfcs/rfc-runtime-support.md § 1 axis A3 row (~line 29) with the same correction

Insert Sysbox as a NET-NEW item 1 in .oh/docs/rfcs/rfc-runtime-support.md § 8 — Sysbox has NO existing entry there today (zero grep hits), so this is an insertion, not a reorder; the seven existing entries (gVisor, Firecracker, Kata, managed sandboxes, CI-as-runtime, deploy-skill family, landscape memo) keep their relative order and renumber down by one
Mark the § 9 'DinD trade-off' open decision as answered, with cross-links to #731, #733, and rfc-brain-hands-boundary.md
No file under .oh/cli/ is modified by this story (docs-only change surface)
Add a CHANGELOG entry under ## [Unreleased] → ### Added for the new RFC
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Define the provider-neutral ExecutionTarget contract
userStories.description: As core orchestration code, I want a narrow capability-oriented execution contract so I can provision, inspect, and execute inside an environment without knowing that Docker exists.
acceptanceCriteria: Create .oh/cli/src/lib/execution/target.ts exporting ExecutionStatus, ExecutionCapability, ExecRequest, ExecResult, and ExecutionTarget
Types and interface ONLY — no implementation and no runtime imports in the file
ExecutionStatus is exactly "absent" | "starting" | "ready" | "stopped" | "failed"
ExecutionCapability is exactly "exec" | "pty" | "files" | "ports" | "docker" | "snapshot"

ExecRequest is { argv: string[]; cwd?: string; env?: Record<string,string>; timeoutMs?: number; stdio?: "inherit" | "capture"; user?: string } — argv, NOT command: string (the codebase bans shell strings)

ExecutionTarget declares readonly kind, readonly contractVersion: 1, readonly workspace: { hostRoot: string; targetRoot: string }, provision?(), status(), capabilities(), exec(), attach?(), destroy?(), describe()
capabilities() returns Promise<ReadonlySet<ExecutionCapability>>

H1 RESOLUTION — attach?() is declared SYNCHRONOUS: `attach?(request: ExecRequest): number`, NOT Promise<number>. provision?(), status(), capabilities(), exec(), and destroy?() stay async. Rationale: LifecycleRunner is already sync ((cmd,args,opts) => RunResult, lifecycle.ts:49-53) over spawnSync (lifecycle.ts:59); attach is a blocking terminal handoff with nothing to await. This is what keeps runShell's public `: number` signature (lifecycle.ts:298) — and therefore US-005's zero-assertion-edit compat oracle against lifecycle.test.ts:362/428/435 — achievable. runSandbox is ALREADY async, so provision(): Promise<void> needs no change; the asymmetry is deliberate
ExecResult is { exitCode: number; stdout: string; stderr: string } with stderr REQUIRED; US-003 is responsible for genuinely populating it (not stubbing it)
The interface declares NO snapshot method — grep for 'snapshot(' in target.ts returns nothing; "snapshot" appears only as a capability literal
target.ts contains no Docker nouns (container, containerId, compose, image, volume, dockerd) except the "docker" capability string literal and its doc comment

A file-header comment records the THREE deliberate refinements to #733's sketch — argv over command:string, the added "absent" status, and the synchronous attach() — with rationale, PLUS the documented migration path that a future contractVersion 2 may make attach() async

The header comment is worded GENERICALLY and contains NO Docker nouns: refinement (1) cites 'the codebase bans shell strings; every subprocess invocation is argv-array form' and refinement (3) cites 'the existing synchronous process-runner seam' — neither names Docker, `docker exec`, containers, compose, or images. Probe C2 bans those nouns file-wide except the "docker" capability literal and its own doc comment, and the header is NOT that comment
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement DockerComposeExecutionTarget by delegating to existing machinery
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the Docker adapter to wrap the proven compose machinery rather than reimplement it, so today's behavior is preserved by construction rather than by luck.
acceptanceCriteria: Create .oh/cli/src/lib/execution/docker-compose-target.ts exporting DockerComposeExecutionTarget implements ExecutionTarget

The adapter delegates compose operations to .oh/scripts/docker-compose.sh; it contains no hand-assembled '-f <overlay>' compose argv list (harness.yaml env, compose overrides, docker-socket opt-in, SSH overlay + port collision checks, Hermes overlay, sandbox naming, project-root behavior all stay in the script)
Create .oh/cli/src/lib/execution/runner.ts holding the LifecycleRunner type and the real spawn runner extracted from .oh/cli/src/commands/lifecycle.ts (~line 49)
.oh/cli/src/commands/lifecycle.ts re-exports LifecycleRunner for back-compat so no existing import path breaks

ORDERING: the extraction reaches its OWN green checkpoint first — with runner.ts plus the lifecycle.ts re-export in place and NO adapter yet, the full existing test suite and typecheck pass. Only then does the adapter land on top (recorded as an intermediate commit or a PR-description note), so the re-export's failure mode cannot be masked by adapter-level green
Create .oh/cli/src/lib/execution/index.ts exporting an INTERNAL resolveExecutionTarget() factory returning a DockerComposeExecutionTarget
No harness.yaml key, CLI flag, or env var is added to select a target (no user-facing selector surface)
capabilities() includes "docker" when the docker-sock overlay is enabled and omits it when the overlay is off

DETECTION MECHANISM (pinned): the adapter determines the overlay state by shelling `.oh/scripts/docker-compose.sh --print-argv` through the injected runner (stdio: "capture") and testing whether the emitted `-f` file list contains a path ending in `docker-compose.docker-sock.yml` (the script appends it at docker-compose.sh:136). The adapter contains NO TypeScript reimplementation of truthy() (docker-compose.sh:63), no harness.yaml parsing for sandbox.docker_socket, and no hardcoded DOCKER_SOCKET env read — the script stays the single source of truth
capabilities() always includes "exec" and "pty"

STDERR (decided): RunResult (lifecycle.ts:38-46) gains `stderr?: string` and spawnRunner populates it from spawnSync's already-piped stderr on stdio:"capture" runs (lifecycle.ts:62 pipes it today and discards it). The change is additive and back-compatible — fake runners that omit stderr still typecheck

exec() returns REAL captured stderr for stdio:"capture" runs, and "" for stdio:"inherit" runs, with a code comment stating that inherited stderr went to the terminal and was never captured (stderr is not a blanket stub)
The adapter accepts an injected runner (DI seam) so tests never spawn a real subprocess
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

Update the runShell doc comment (.oh/cli/src/commands/lifecycle.ts:291-296) to describe attach()-based delegation, not a literal `docker exec` invocation

runShell KEEPS its exact public signature `export function runShell(opts: ShellOptions, io: LifecycleIO): number` — not async, not returning a Promise (git diff on that signature line shows only the body changing). This is possible because attach() is sync in contractVersion 1 (US-002). userStories.title: Prove no regression — tests + tier-A probe
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I need mechanical proof that the abstraction changed no operator behavior, so I can approve the seam without re-reasoning about Docker.
acceptanceCriteria: Create .oh/cli/src/__tests__/execution-target.test.ts using a fake runner (no real subprocess spawned)
It asserts exact argv for provision() and attach()
It asserts capability discovery in BOTH socket states: overlay on → set contains "docker"; overlay off → set omits "docker"
It exercises stdio: "inherit" streaming, not only "capture" (a capture-only suite would silently drop live build output and interactive shells)

It contains a MINIMAL exec() unit test so exec() does not ship as dead, unverified surface: with a fake runner returning { status: 0, stdout: "hi", stderr: "warn" }, exec() resolves to { exitCode: 0, stdout: "hi", stderr: "warn" } — proving argv pass-through AND that stderr is genuinely plumbed per US-003 rather than hardcoded

COMPAT ORACLE (kept at full strength): every existing assertion in .oh/cli/src/__tests__/lifecycle.test.ts passes UNCHANGED — zero assertion edits, git diff on that file shows no changed expectations, and no await/async/rejects rewrites of the runShell cases. This is achievable because attach() is sync in contractVersion 1 (US-002), keeping expect(runShell(...)).toBe(0) (lifecycle.test.ts:362, :428) and expect(() => runShell(...)).toThrow(...) (:435) valid

Add a case to .oh/scripts/__tests__/compose-args.test.ts asserting adapter-produced compose argv is identical to today's argv, using `.oh/scripts/docker-compose.sh --print-argv` as the non-executing oracle
Create executable tier-A probe .oh/evals/probes/execution-target-contract.sh with the standard 3-state PASS/REGRESSION/SKIPPED oracle and exactly five checks
Probe C1: .oh/cli/src/lib/execution/target.ts exists
Probe C2: target.ts contains no Docker nouns (excepting the "docker" capability literal)
Probe C3: target.ts declares no snapshot method

Probe C4: runShell in .oh/cli/src/commands/lifecycle.ts contains no direct docker exec argv. MATCHING STRATEGY (pinned): C4 inspects argv LITERALS passed to the runner — it asserts no ["exec", "-it", ...] argv array is constructed outside the adapter — and is NOT a naive text grep of the file, so surviving comments and doc prose can neither trip C4 nor falsely satisfy it

Probe C5: Makefile still contains, VERBATIM, the whole line `docker exec -it -u $(SHELL_USER) $(SHELL_CONTAINER) zsh` — an exact whole-line match, NOT a loose `grep -q "docker exec"` (which would stay green through an argument-level regression)
Probe C2 is DRY-RUN against the FINAL committed target.ts header text before this story is called done, proving the generically-worded header (US-002) does not trip the Docker-noun ban
Verify the probe by rejection: it exits non-zero when target.ts is edited to mention a container, not merely green on the finished branch
bash .oh/evals/probes/execution-target-contract.sh is green in a full /eval run
